messages:
Olivia (Support): FYI escalated from Acme-CSE — since the policy UI push they see auth failures + duplicate billing. Their traffic which should stick to us-east is getting fanned out to eu-west and eu-central, causing retries and duplicate token exchanges. Request example: req_x9f3a2b4.
Ken (Routing Eng): @Olivia can you paste the exact failover policy they had and the one currently applied? any chance weights/priorities flipped? :eyes:
Acme-CSE: Here's what we applied (copied from console right after the incident):
```
{"failover_policy": [{"region":"eu-west-1","priority":2,"weight":20},{"region":"us-east-1","priority":1,"weight":80}], "sticky_ttl": 0}
```
Olivia (Support): Console shows sticky_ttl 0 for this customer now, but before it was 3600. They say they didn't change TTL.
Maya (Infra): Deploy bot shows a config schema change merged just before the incident window. @deploy-bot details?
deploy-bot: PR #4321 merged by ken at 2026-03-15T08:57:12Z — change: stringifyPolicy() now applies a key-sorting step for stable diffs.
Ken (Routing Eng): Oh. The key-sorting was intended for diffing but probably reorders array elements when policy is round-tripped through our console. If priorities are relied on by array position we can break ordering. I'll check parser.
Liam (SRE): Symptoms align with sticky becoming 0 -> no session affinity -> requests go to weighted selection across all eligible regions. If the array got reordered so eu entries are earlier we could see initial hits to EU and then retries back to US when auth fails. That explains auth token exchange spikes and duplicate charges.
Ken (Routing Eng): Reproduced locally: console serialize -> server parse changed the priority semantics. Also weight fields were being parsed as strings in one path; e.g. "80" became 8 in a decimal parse fallback and then normalized -> equal weights. Repro steps:
1) push policy via console (same UI payload)
2) read back via API -> array order differs
3) issue a signed request with session cookie -> cookie TTL dropped to 0 in returned policy -> no affinity
Command I used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Policy-Version: v3" -d '{"policy":...}' https://internal-api/redwood/v1/policies/apply
```
Ken (Routing Eng): Minimal repro attached: small script that round-trips policy over the console layer and shows ordering flip.
Acme-CSE: We also observed a ton of 401s for a short window and then many duplicate idempotent charges — we had to refund some transactions.
Maya (Infra): Rolling back PR #4321 in canary now. Liam will coordinate rollback to prod after verification.
Liam (SRE): Rolling back canary at 2026-03-15T09:30Z. Monitoring egress auth errors and accepted region headers. Initial telemetry shows eu->us ratio returning to expected. :thumbsup:
Ken (Routing Eng): Patch plan: remove key-sorting for policy stringify, add explicit deterministic ordering based on "priority" field (not arbitrary key sort), and ensure weight is parsed with Number() and validated range 0-100. Add unit + integration test for console round-trip.
Olivia (Support): I've escalated billing impact to finance and customer success. Ticket created: FIN-9876 for reconciliation and refunds.
Maya (Infra): Postmortem stub: PMT-2026-03-15-eu-fanout-auth — need timeline, root cause (console stringify reorder + TTL override), blast radius, and follow-ups (parser fix, tests, canary policy).
Ken (Routing Eng): Temporary mitigation: for any policy apply path we will honor existing sticky_ttl if the incoming payload sets it to 0 but the previous policy had >0, until fix is deployed. I'll open hotfix PR.
Acme-CSE: Thanks team, please share when rollback completes and if we need to rotate keys. We started short TTL rotation to limit replays.
Liam (SRE): Rollback completed to prod at 2026-03-15T10:05Z. Monitoring looks good, auth failures dropped to baseline, customer confirms.
Olivia (Support): Closing the immediate escalation. Next steps: Ken to land parser fix + tests, Maya to run billing reconciliation with FIN-9876, create follow-up to improve canary guardrails so console schema changes can't flip array semantics.
Ken (Routing Eng): PR #4335 opened for parser fix, added test cases for: preserved priority order, numeric weight parsing, and sticky_ttl retention. Will request review.
Maya (Infra): Also adding observability alert for sudden sticky_ttl -> 0 changes per customer to catch regressions earlier.
Olivia (Support): Thanks all. I'll update Acme-CSE and confirm refunds. :white_check_mark:
